Main
================================================================================

Mike L. Smith {#title}
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data Management Coordinator - European Molecular Biology Laboratory.

My current role involves supporting the needs of EMBL's large-scale data generation and collection 
activities, identifying and addressing technical issues to improve data handling practice.

As part of the EMBL Data Science Centre, I work closely with researchers, 
scientific core facilities, IT services, and other data management experts to 
harmonise efforts in large-scale biological data management across EMBL’s 
international sites.  My team and I develop and deploy tools, workflows and 
best practice protocols to streamline data processes and maximise the utility of 
EMBL’s research data.

I am also passionate about research software engineering and good software practices for 
reproducible research. I work extensively with version control, containers,
and literate programming tools like R Markdown, champion these practices to
those around me, and have taught multiple courses on these topics.

Professional Experience {data-icon=laptop} 
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data Management Coordinator

European Molecular Biology Laboratory

Heidelberg, DE

2023-

- Leading a small, internationally distributed, team focused on improving
data management across the laboratory, from production to deposition
in public repositories.
- Coordinating the implementation of standardised, high-throughput, data processing 
pipelines using containerized software and workflow languages, such as Nextflow and Snakemake, 
in HPC and cloud computing environments.
- Establishing best practices for metadata standards and documentation to enhance data usability,
in particular by following the FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) data principles.
- Experience with the data management requirements for a range of
biological data modalities, including sequencing, microscopy imaging, and
x-ray crystallography.
- Recruiting, setting objectives, appraising, and mentoring direct reports in the 
data management team.
- Providing consultation services to scientists and project managers to construct and implement 
data management plans, meeting the requirements of both grant funding agencies
and researchers working at the bench.
- Overseeing how research data is stored, structured, and archived for accessibility and long-term preservation.
- Delivering training and workshops on data management best practices
- Ensuring compliance with institutional and funding agency data policies
- Coordinating with staff at regional partners in the Health + Life Science Alliance
Heidelberg Mannheim to develop a platform proposal for data sharing and collaboration
between institutions

### Senior Scientific Programmer

European Molecular Biology Laboratory

Heidelberg, DE

2019-23

- Identified the need for Zarr support in R and created [Rarr]([grimbough/bioc-actions](https://github.com/grimbough/Rarr)), the first R/Zarr interface.
- Developed and deployed [Bioconductor Code Tools](https://code.bioconductor.org/) website.  Using Docker containers and a Kubernetes deployment, this site provides tools for browsing and searching the code behind all Bioconductor packages.
- Designed and maintained Bioconductor GitHub Actions to simplify using GitHub actions for BioC package development - [grimbough/bioc-actions](https://github.com/grimbough/bioc-actions)
- Ported HDF5 compression filters to R via [rhdf5filters](https://bioconductor.org/packages/rhdf5filters) & benchmarked their performance on single-cell data.
- Created a continuous integration workflow using GitHub Actions for the Quarto book [Modern Statistics for Modern Biology](https://www.huber.embl.de/msmb/). This rapidly builds chapters in parallel, deploys a new edition of the book if successful, and alerts authors via email if any problems are encountered.
- Organised and hosted monthly Bioconductor Developer Forum and embl-R discussion sessions
- Mentored junior software developers, both within EMBL and the wider community, to improve their R skills and develop their own packages.


### Bioinformatician

European Molecular Biology Laboratory

Heidelberg, DE

2015-19

- Maintained and continued development of several widely used Bioconductor packages with extensive userbases and thousands of downloads per month e.g. [biomaRt](https://bioconductor.org/packages/biomaRt/) and [rhdf5](https://bioconductor.org/packages/rhdf5/). This involved:
  - Modernising and strengthening the code base via code review & development of unit tests
  - Updating documentation and vignettes
  - Providing end-user support via email, online forums, and GitHub issues
- Collaborated with experimental biologists to develop software for the analysis of pooled CRISPR screens
- Developed workflows for analysis of bulk RNA-seq data, deployed on an HPC cluster

## Publications {data-icon=book}

<div class="references">

```{r, echo = FALSE, results='asis', warning=FALSE}
bib <- bib2df::bib2df("references/works.bib") |> 
  dplyr::arrange(desc(YEAR))
me_first <- vapply(bib$AUTHOR, function(x) { grepl(pattern = "Smith", x[1]) }, 
                   FUN.VALUE = logical(1)) 
print_cite <- function(x) { sprintf("- %s. *%s*. %s (%s)", 
                                    paste(unlist(x$AUTHOR), collapse = ", "), 
                                    x$TITLE,
                                    x$JOURNAL,
                                    x$YEAR) }

cat("<h3>First Author</h3>\n")

cat(apply(bib |> dplyr::filter(me_first), 1, print_cite), sep = "\n")

cat("\n<h3>Contributing Author</h3>\n")
cat(apply(bib |> dplyr::filter(!me_first), 1, print_cite), sep = "\n")

```


</div>
